entries.subject: fix(spoiler-guard): keep a neutral Path on guarded items so Download works
entries.notes: The C# file moved, it was not rewritten: upstream’s hunks to Services/SpoilerGuard/SpoilerFieldStripFilter.cs apply at Shared/SpoilerGuard/SpoilerFieldStripFilter.cs, its test hunks at tests/backend/Features/SpoilerGuard/PrivacyFieldFilterTests.cs, and the docs hunk as is. Differences from upstream: (1) the neutral path’s extension. Upstream appends the item’s Container as it is, and for some files that is ffprobe’s whole format list (33 of the lab’s 3,000 episodes: every .mp4 has “mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2”), so the file name jellyfin-web builds for Download is “Oswald S01E03.mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2” (seen on upstream’s build on the lab). Here the extension is the name in that list the file itself uses (“mp4”), else the list’s first name; only a name from the list is ever used, never text of the real path, so a path such as “Show.S02E03.Secret.Ending” gives nothing away. For a one-name Container the result is upstream’s. Filed as a found bug against upstream. (2) NeutralPath sits above the comment block that documents ShouldStrip, where upstream’s hunk puts it between that comment and ShouldStrip. (3) One test theory is added to upstream’s (six cases through the filter’s real entry, on the single-item route and the episode list: an .mkv, the .mp4 list, a list name in another case, a path whose last dot is part of the title, no container, and a second pass over the same DTO changing nothing). Kept from upstream as it is: a guarded movie’s neutral path is “/Item.<ext>” and a season’s “/<Series> E02”; neither is read by Download all, which reads the episodes’. The access question: Path was removed and is now a made-up value built from the series name, the season and episode numbers and a container name, all of which the guarded DTO already carries; no spoiler check is loosened. entries.subject: fix(leaving-soon): page through every Maintainerr collection member
entries.notes: The C# file moved, it was not rewritten: upstream’s hunks to Services/LeavingSoonService.cs apply at Features/MediaTags/Services/LeavingSoonService.cs (the guard is Shared.Arr.ArrUrlGuard here) and are then changed. Kept from upstream: GetJsonAsync (one guarded GET: address guard, key header, 30-second timeout, no redirect followed, 16 MiB), the request GET /api/collections/media/{id}/content/{page}?size=500 for each active collection with a numeric id, at most 40 pages, the stop rule (page × 500 reaches totalSize, or a page without rows; a short page is not the last) and ParseCollections’ third parameter. Differences from upstream: (1) a failed page fails the refresh. Upstream catches every failure of a collection’s paging except a cancellation and falls back to the few embedded members without recording a failure, so one failed page takes the badge off the rest (on upstream’s build on the lab, 971 members: the second page of one collection answers HTTP 500 once and the status reads 353 items, no failure). Here only a 404 for a collection’s first page (a Maintainerr without the route) falls back to its embedded members; any other failure is the refresh’s failure, which keeps the previous answer and retries with the existing delays (the same run on the port: 971 items kept, last failure “HTTP 500”). (2) An answer of the paged route that is not an object with an items array is refused (“not a Maintainerr collections answer”); upstream reads it as a collection without members. (3) The paged members add to the embedded ones, they do not replace them: Maintainerr leaves a row out of a page when it cannot read that row’s metadata, so a member the list itself names stays one (on upstream’s build a page answered as {totalSize: 351, items: []} takes the badge off all 351 movies, the two the list embeds included; here those two keep it). (4) An id that is not a number: upstream calls TryGetInt32 on it, which throws for a string, so a list with such a collection fails the whole refresh (“request failed”) where the code before read its embedded members; here that collection is read from its embedded members and not asked for pages. totalSize has the same guard. (5) Only entries the parser recognises as collections are asked for pages, each id once, and the list’s unwrapping (data/items/collections/results) is one function for the parser and the paging, where upstream repeats it. (6) docs/enhanced/tags.md and docs/advanced/api.md describe the paged requests and their failure rule; upstream’s commit changes no docs. (7) Tests. Upstream’s commit has none and leaves its own LeavingSoonTests failing (9 of 47 at 53ebf043, run here: its fixture answers the collections list on every path, which the new code reads as a collection without members). Here the fixture gets the paged route (404 unless a test sets it) and three tests are added, all through RefreshAsync against the fixture server: 1,100 members over three pages with a short page, a collection answered without totalSize, an inactive one never asked for, ids that are missing or not numbers, the key and base path on every request; the pages adding to the embedded members, and the 404 fallback; twelve ways a page can fail or not be one, each keeping the last good answer with its reason and reaching no other host, a totalSize that is not a number, and a cancellation between pages. Two existing expectations change because a refresh now asks for pages too (the key test lists both requests; the redirect test’s “every request went to /api/collections” becomes a prefix check), and the fixture’s Requests counts the list requests, so the refresh-count assertions stand as they were. Kept from upstream as it is: members beyond 20,000 per collection are not read; a row that a page leaves out and the list does not embed is not a member; when a page comes back without rows, the members the list does not embed lose their badge until the next refresh. The access question: the new requests go only to the administrator’s configured Maintainerr origin, through the same guard, with the same key header, never following a redirect; nothing a user can read changes shape. No setting, route, authorization or registration changes; the snapshot layout and the tag-cache schema are unchanged.

entries.subject: fix(activity): show plays and favorites of versions, people and genres (#1042)
entries.notes: The C# file moved, it was not rewritten: upstream’s Services/ActivityFeedBuilder.cs is Features/Activity/Services/ActivityFeedBuilder.cs here, and before this commit the rewrite’s file was upstream’s with its Jellyfin 12 branches taken (checked: identical after removing the #if lines and the 10.11 branches). The port is upstream’s Jellyfin 12 code as it is: PermittedIds (the user-scoped query with GroupByPresentationUniqueKey off), ResolveHiddenVersions (a denied id that passes the same query with IncludeOwnedItems, shown as its primary version or owner when that item passes the ordinary query), PermittedByNameIds (favorites only; IncludeItemTypes names the five by-name kinds; an item with a ParentId stays under the library rule), one Watched and one Favorited row per person and title (the newest row, the highest progress, any completion), and MergeLaterVersionPlays for watches past the page that filled the feed. Differences from upstream: (1) Jellyfin 12 only. This tree has no 10.11 build, so upstream’s #if !JF12 lines (the 10.11 query and its two empty lookups) and its 10.11 test (OnJellyfin1011TheFeedKeepsItsOneLibraryQueryAndByNameFavoritesStayHidden) are left out; nothing else differs in the code. (2) Tests: upstream’s tests/backend/Privacy/ActivityFeedHiddenItemsTests.cs is tests/backend/Features/Activity/ActivityFeedHiddenItemsTests.cs here (namespace JE.Tests.Features.Activity, the builder’s namespace, no #if), its ten Jellyfin 12 tests unchanged; five of them fail on the tree before the port. (3) Docs: the two paragraphs (docs/advanced/api.md, docs/enhanced/enhanced-features.md) without “On Jellyfin 12” and the 10.11 sentence, since these pages describe a Jellyfin 12 plugin. (4) The entry’s guessed feature hidden-content was wrong (the word in the test file’s name): the change is in activity only. Kept from upstream as it is: a failing alternate-version or by-name lookup hides only those rows and logs a warning, the ordinary rows still load (those rows were always hidden before, and showing them without the access answer would be the worse fault); when a shown Watched row is partial, the unread watches of its author are run through the same access queries, 64 at a time (activity.json holds at most 500 entries). The access question: every new row passes a query scoped by Jellyfin for the viewer (library roots, parental and tag rules), for the version and for the title on the card, and by-name favorites pass Jellyfin’s own by-name rule; on the lab the rows each of five users gets (an administrator, two plain users, one with a parental limit, one with the Movies library only) are the same on upstream’s build and on the port, and the people, genres and studios each gets are the ones Jellyfin’s own item query returns to that user. activity.json is not changed: it keeps the id that was played or favorited. No setting, route, authorization or registration changes.

entries.subject: fix(leaving-soon): fall back to the embedded members when the paged endpoint answers something else, update request counts
entries.notes: The paging loop in Features/MediaTags/Services/LeavingSoonService.cs is the rewrite’s own since the port of 53ebf043 (cf86e164), so upstream’s two product lines are re-implemented, not applied. Upstream: an answer of the paged route that is not an object with an items array now throws inside the collection’s catch-all, so that collection is read from the members the list embeds (before, it was read as a collection without members). Here the rewrite refused such an answer as a failed refresh (“not a Maintainerr collections answer”); now, for a collection’s first page, it is read as a source without the paged route, as a 404 already was: the collection keeps the members the list embeds, no failure is recorded, and the other collections are still read page by page. On the lab, a source that answers the collections list on every address: 0 items and that failure before the port; 4 items, no failure, two movie cards with “Leaving in 20d” and the same three requests on upstream’s build and on the port. Differences from upstream: (1) only the first page. A later page that is not a page, after a first one that was, stays a failed refresh that keeps the previous answer (difference 1 of the 53ebf043 entry). Upstream throws away the pages it read and carries on with the embedded members, recording nothing (on upstream’s build on the lab, 971 members: the second page of one collection answers the collections list once and the status reads 353 items, no failure; the port keeps 971 with that failure). Filed as a found bug. (2) A first page that is not JSON at all (an empty body, HTML) stays a failed refresh, as the 53ebf043 entry has it; upstream falls back there too, since 53ebf043. (3) docs/enhanced/tags.md and docs/advanced/api.md state the rule; upstream’s commit changes no docs. (4) Tests. Upstream’s commit changes only expectations of its own tests, to fit its fixture, which answers the collections list on every path: the key test checks the first request and the key on all of them, the redirect test’s path check becomes a prefix check, and four request counts in two tests grow by the page requests (its LeavingSoonTests pass again: 47 of 47 at 8fe1e705, run here). The rewrite’s fixture has the paged route (404 unless a test sets it) and counts the list requests, so those expectations stand as they are. One test is added, through RefreshAsync against the fixture server, failing before the port (LastError “not a Maintainerr collections answer” where none is expected): a collection whose first page is not a page keeps its embedded member while the other collection is still paged; then eight JSON answers that are no page (the collections list again, as upstream’s fixture answers, an array, objects without an items array, null, a string, a number) each give the embedded members without a failure, after one page request per collection, the key on every request. In the existing failure test the row “the first page answers []” (a failed refresh until now) is replaced by two first pages that are not JSON (an empty body, HTML), which stay failures. Kept from upstream as it is: on a source that pages, a first page answered with JSON that is no page shortens that collection to its embedded members until the next refresh, as a 404 for it already did (lab: 622 of 971 on both builds; 971 with a failure before the port). No setting, route, authorization or registration changes; the snapshot layout and the tag-cache schema are unchanged, and no version constant covers the change.

entries.subject: feat(player): open the native playback info overlay from the shortcut, keep plugin overlay as fallback
entries.notes: Re-implemented in client/src/features/player/playback-info.ts. As upstream: the ShowPlaybackInfo shortcut first toggles jellyfin-web’s own stats panel through the “Playback Info” entry (data-id="stats") of the OSD settings menu, while a style keeps .dialogContainer, .dialogBackdrop and .actionSheet invisible until 400 ms after the attempt; the plugin overlay is the fallback when the settings button or that entry is missing or the attempt throws (same warning). The next press toggles the native panel off the same way, or closes the plugin overlay if that is open. On the lab (Chromium) the port and upstream’s build show the same: the native panel with 16 rows after the first press, hidden after the second, no plugin overlay, nothing left behind; before the port the plugin overlay opened. Differences from upstream: (1) The menu is driven with the track menus’ helpers from native-track-menu.ts (createTrackMenu now returns them, and openOsdMenu takes its timeout, 1.5 s here as upstream’s budget): the new sheet is awaited with JE.core.dom.waitForElement instead of a requestAnimationFrame loop, and the button and the entry get a pointerdown before the click. jellyfin-web’s video OSD in Firefox drops a click whose target does not contain the target of the last keydown or pointerdown, so upstream’s plain .click() after the key press never opens the menu there: on the lab in Firefox upstream’s build shows the plugin overlay after its 1.5 s wait, the port the native panel. (2) A menu without the entry is closed the way dialogHelper accepts, pointerdown, mousedown and click on its .dialogContainer. Upstream clicks a .dialogBackdrop inside the container, but jellyfin-web 12.4 puts the backdrop before the container, so nothing is clicked: on the lab, with the entry removed as the sheet is built, upstream’s build leaves the settings menu open and visible beside the plugin overlay, and still after the overlay is closed again; the port closes it unseen and opens the overlay. (3) A second press while the menu is still opening is ignored. Upstream starts a second attempt: on the lab in Firefox, a second press during upstream’s 1.5 s wait left two plugin overlays, the first one no longer referenced and never removed. And when the player is left while the menu opens no overlay follows (the wait ends with the player’s lifetime and the press’s lease is checked). The hiding style is removed by a plain timer, not one of the player lifetime’s, so a navigation cannot cancel its removal. (4) docs/enhanced/enhanced-features.md says what the shortcut does now; upstream’s docs still say it toggles JE’s overlay. Differences 1 to 4 are filed as one found bug. Kept from upstream as it is: jellyfin-web logs “ActionSheet closed without resolving” as a page error when the fallback closes the menu, as it does when a person closes any sheet by clicking beside it; a menu that opens only after the 1.5 s wait is not closed (upstream the same). Tests: upstream’s commit adds none. tests/frontend/features/player/features-playback-info.test.mjs presses the key through enhanced/events.js into enhanced/player/playback.js with the real core/dom-observer.js, against a stand-in for jellyfin-web’s OSD menu modelled on what the lab showed (the backdrop beside the container, closing only for a mousedown and click on the container, Firefox’s click guard): native panel on and off with the menu hidden while open, Firefox, a menu without the entry, no settings button, a second press while the menu opens, leaving the player. Five fail before the port; the one without a settings button describes behaviour that does not change. No setting, string, route, authorization or registration changes; nothing stored or cached changes.

entries.subject: fix(seerr): Seerr routes follow the caller's library access and Jellyfin's parental rules (#1055)
entries.notes: Upstream squashes the seven commits of its PR branch fix/seerr-access. Their first versions landed here first, as the rewrite's own commits: fc27dc69 (studio/, genre/, boxset/ and items/by-providers resolve the item through the caller; Features/Seerr/JeSeerrController.Discover.cs GetItemForCaller, Features/Calendar/JeCalendarController.cs), 63e5d7ef with c2197790 (person/ through the same helper), a1786432 (the certification falls back to the US one, and for a series the first listed; scored in the server's country first; Shared/Parental/SeerrCertificationExtractor.cs, SeerrParentalFilter.cs), 989f3c0b (a sub-score limit applies only at its own score; Shared/Parental/ParentalRatingDecision.cs), 087ff84d (the request list filter is escaped; JeSeerrController.Requests.cs) and 0304f12e (override rules answered [] without a Seerr call for a linked user who is not a Seerr admin; JeSeerrController.cs), with their auth-read contract lines (bc86d499). Those parts are not repeated. Ported here is what upstream's versions changed since: (1) studios, genres and persons are answered to any signed-in caller, as Jellyfin's /Studios/{name}, /Genres/{name} and /Persons/{name} routes and JE's people/info answer them; Jellyfin's user item overload hides an untagged studio or genre (and on 10.11 a person) from a user with an Allowed Tags list, which took the studio and genre discovery rows away from that user here. Titles and box sets still go through the caller. GetItemForCaller is upstream's, in this tree's controller partial. (2) A series' certification is picked exactly as Jellyfin's TmdbSeriesProvider picks it: the country's first entry, else the first US entry, else the first listed, and the entry picked decides, so an empty rating there leaves the title unrated (the rewrite's a1786432 tried every country and US entry and skipped empty ones, so a DE "" / US TV-MA series was scored TV-MA here and unrated in the library); an entry with no rating at all is passed over, as Jellyfin 12 does. (3) items/by-providers checks visibility for at most the first 100 matches for a non-administrator. (4) The comment that said Seerr does not gate /api/v1/overrideRule, and the extractor and filter comments, as upstream. (5) Docs: docs/advanced/api.md (the rating paragraph, jellyseerr/request, jellyseerr/overrideRule, studio/, boxset/, genre/, person/, items/by-providers rows and the by-providers paragraph) and docs/seerr/seerr-features.md (the rating pick) applied as is with git apply; tests/docs/coverage-matrix.md gets upstream's two sentences with this tree's test file names. entries.subject: fix(hidden-content): saves keep changes made elsewhere and never replace a list that failed to load (#1056)
entries.notes: Upstream squashes the ten commits of its PR branch fix/hidden-content-saves. The first versions of five landed here first, as the rewrite's own commits, and are not repeated: 3d6c27f1 (a hidden list or shortcut list that failed to load stays null; Hidden Content refuses edits and never posts it; the shortcut editor stays read-only; the bootstrap and GET hidden-content.json / shortcuts.json read strictly, null / 500), f211f861 (each save reads the stored list and writes only this session's changes onto it; a Continue Watching / Next Up hide the server wrote is recorded as stored; saves run one at a time through enqueueWrite and flushPendingSave waits for a write in flight), 8518a722 (only the document's own pagehide stops the save retry, Status Tags and the settings panel), e38864fc (the Seerr card passes the plain title; names stored escaped read as plain text) and 92286fb2 (Manage Hidden Content opens the management dialog when the page is a tab or Plugin Page). Ported here is what upstream's versions changed since or add: (1) an edit refused because the list is not loaded says so (toast hidden_content_not_loaded, a new en.json string), confirmAndHide refuses before asking anything, and a settings panel switch whose change is refused goes back without running its side effects (dede014d); (2) the save's merge (model.ts withChanges): an entry the session read and changed or removed also reaches the server's copy of it under the other ID spelling, which the session never read, while keys the session read and left alone stay (fixup 9df8e43d and fb08398c): here an unhide right after Remove from Continue Watching left the entry the server stored under the dashed ID, so the item stayed out of Continue Watching; (3) a save with nothing of the session's to write posts nothing (upstream's first version); (4) each request of a save fails after 30 s, so a save that gets no answer is retried instead of holding later saves and a Continue Watching / Next Up removal, which is refused with its message (885e0198); (5) names stored HTML-escaped still read as plain text, but a save of other changes no longer rewrites them: the save merges onto the list as stored and the session reads names plain (model.ts withPlainNames); (6) refresh() keeps changes not saved yet on top of the list it reads; (7) the page's showPage() says whether it showed, and the Manage button uses that, so Plugin Pages chosen but not installed opens the page again (the rewrite opened the dialog) (0aefa637); (8) GET hidden-content.json, GET shortcuts.json and the bootstrap set content that does not parse aside to .corrupt-<ts> once, so the next read starts from the defaults (upstream's first version and e06003bd); here the strict read already holds the file's lock for the read and the move, leaves a file it could not open in place, and every save (shortcuts included) already takes that lock, so this is quarantineCorrupt on those three reads; the 500 messages are upstream's; (9) docs/enhanced/enhanced-features.md and docs/advanced/api.md applied with git apply, the bootstrap lines saying null as this tree's bootstrap writes it; the coverage-matrix row names this tree's tests. Tests: upstream's features-hidden-save.test.mjs and features-hidden-manage-button.test.mjs run against this tree's built modules in tests/frontend/features/hidden-content/, upstream's ApiUserDocumentReadTests is tests/backend/Features/Platform/ApiUserDocumentReadTests.cs, and its server-shape bootstrap test is in tests/frontend/bootstrap/bootstrap.test.mjs. On the branch's start 9 of the 33 frontend tests in the two new files fail (one per behaviour above) and 3 of the 19 backend tests in ApiUserDocumentReadTests and BootstrapContractTests; all pass after. Existing tests changed: BootstrapContractTests.UnreadableHiddenListAndShortcutsAreReportedAsFailedNotEmpty expected the unparseable files left in place and now expects them set aside once, then the defaults; seven Undo tests (HC-R4B-001 x3 in features-hidden-regressions, two in features-hidden-rewrite and two in tests/browser/hidden-content-rewrite.spec.cjs) undid a hide before any save and checked the POST, which (3) no longer sends, so each saves the hide first and checks the Undo's write. Differences from upstream: (a) a refused edit throws here after the message, as since 3d6c27f1 (its tests assert it), where upstream's returns false; for the user it is the same: the message, nothing asked, nothing saved. (b) This tree keeps one entry per item: an unhide removes every entry stored for the same item ID and a hide merges them (since its first version; 'GUID unhide removes equivalent storage aliases'). Upstream keeps a Continue Watching entry and a hide of the same item as separate entries, each removed on its own (fb08398c); its two tests for that are not ported, its server-shape test unhides a plain entry here, and this is filed for a decision (je12 found-bug NEW-20261113-135220). (c) Upstream's client reads a document left out of the bootstrap as not loaded (fixup d2b8feb8), because Jellyfin's serializer omits nulls; this tree's bootstrap writes the nulls (TransportJson) and a bootstrap without a document fails its contract and falls back to the per-document reads, so nothing changes; a test shows it. (d) Upstream reads an unparseable list again under the file's lock before moving it; here the only read is under the lock, so its second-read test is replaced by one where the read waits on the lock. No route, verb, authorization or registration changes; the Architecture snapshots pass unchanged. Nothing stored changes shape; no cached-output version moves.

entries.subject: Translations update from Hosted Weblate (#1057)
entries.notes: Applied as is (git show 31969cba | git apply --3way, clean): the 32 locale files under Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyfinEnhanced/js/locales/ are byte-identical to upstream's at 31969cba. It adds one key to each, hidden_content_not_loaded, the message of the Hidden Content saves follow-ups (#1056, ported here as row 40) shown when an edit is refused because the hidden list did not load. Every one of the 32 values is the English source text, the same as en.json here and upstream (Weblate seeding a new key), so a user reads what the English fallback already gave them. No key changes or goes; the value has no {placeholders}; the key exists in this tree's en.json. No key the server reads for poster tag captions (StatusRules) changes, so no resolver version moves. No difference from upstream.
